run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T07:03:51Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is explained by a rollout restart of the ad and payment Deployments at 2026-11-17T07:02:17Z: each had a single pod, the old pod was terminated, and the replacement containers — CPU-limited to 50m (ad) and 20m (payment) — spent minutes starting while the Services' ClusterIPs refused connections. The frontend's error spans rise in step: GET and GET /api/data fail with HTTP 500 because grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds returns '14 UNAVAILABLE ... connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080' (the ad Service ClusterIP), and POST /api/checkout fails because checkout reports 'failed to charge card ... dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused' (the payment Service ClusterIP). The ad container logged 'Ad service starting.' only at 07:06:44 and 'listening on 8080' at 07:08:38 — 6m19s after its 07:02:19 container start — while its CPU usage sat exactly at its 50m limit with 100% of CFS periods throttled from 07:04:30 to 07:08:30. Frontend error-span rate peaked at 0.8667/s at 07:07:51 and was 0 at the 07:14:51 evaluation. The ad leg dominates (its error series is identical to frontend GET), the payment leg is smaller and ended earlier (payment served its first Charge at 07:03:57). Both pods are now Running/ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, so this was a slow startup, not a crash, OOM or eviction; no other pod in otel-demo restarted. The non-default flagd flags adFailure="on" and paymentFailure="100%" were considered as the cause and rejected: the observed failures are TCP connection refusals at the Service ClusterIPs, not application-level flag errors, and frontend error rate was 0 from 07:14:51 while the ConfigMap still declares both faults at 07:20:32.

claims.text: Frontend error-status span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR) was 0 at every returned point from 06:45:00 through the 07:03:00 evaluation, peaked at 0.8667 spans/s at the 07:07:51 evaluation, and was 0 at the 07:14:51, 07:15:51 and 07:16:51 evaluations. The GET and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds series carry identical values, and the POST / POST /api/checkout / grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder series form a second, smaller curve that reaches 0 by the 07:10:00 point.

At the 07:03:51 instant, frontend error spans were on GET (0.0444/s), executing api route (pages) /api/data (0.0444/s), grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (0.0444/s), POST and executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (0.0333/s each) and tcp.connect (0.0259/s); in the same result grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem and the cart API routes had no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series (cart routes at 0).

The frontend error spans carry HTTP 500 and the dependency errors verbatim: grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds has rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080'; grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder has rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'. These spans start at 07:03:23–07:03:26 in the sampled trace view.

100.65.180.246 is the ClusterIP of Service ad (port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad) and 100.70.188.60 is the ClusterIP of Service payment in namespace otel-demo, so the refused connections were to those two Services' ClusterIPs, not to pod IPs.

Events in otel-demo at 07:02:17–07:02:21 show Deployments ad and payment scaling up new ReplicaSets: ad-6cb57f76d scaled 0->1 and pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 Started at 07:02:19, old pod ad-554b849958-mbnxm 'Killing – Stopping container ad' at 07:02:20 with ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 SuccessfulDelete and scaled 1->0; payment-9c8ffb665 scaled 0->1 with pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 Started at 07:02:20, old pod payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb killed at 07:02:21.

The two new ReplicaSet pod templates (ad-6cb57f76d, payment-9c8ffb665) differ from the previous ones only by the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T07:02:17Z: same images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and :2.1.3-payment, same env, no livenessProbe and no readinessProbe, resources limits ad cpu 50m/memory 450Mi and payment cpu 20m/memory 160Mi. This is a rollout restart with an unchanged pod template.

In pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 the container's first log line in the window is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-17T07:06:44.827465751Z and the next is 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 2026-11-17T07:08:38.226369917Z, while the container state shows running startedAt 2026-11-17T07:02:19Z; request log lines begin at 07:09:24.

While the ad container started, its throttled-CFS-period ratio was 0.864 and 0.935 at 07:03:00/07:03:30, then 0.945 at 07:04:00 and exactly 1.0 at every returned point from 07:04:30 to 07:08:30, falling to 0.74 at 07:09:00 and 0.405 at 07:10:00; its CPU usage rate was pinned at ~0.049 cores (the 50m limit) from 07:04:00 through 07:08:00.

In pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 there are no payment log lines between 07:02:10 and 07:03:57; the first is 'Charge request received.' at 2026-11-17T07:03:57.025Z, and its CPU usage rate was ~0.020 cores (the 20m limit) at 07:03:00–07:04:30, dropping to ~0.008 afterwards.

The only non-zero error series for the checkout service were oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge with identical values (0.1494 at 07:05:00, 0.1375, 0.132, 0.1222, 0.0074, then 0 from 07:10:00), i.e. checkout's error is its payment leg, and it ends well before the frontend's ad-related error curve.

frontend-proxy's own error spans rose in step with the frontend failures: span ingress went from a ~0.0037–0.0148/s baseline to 1.0037/s at 07:07:51 and 'router frontend egress' to 1.0037/s at the same point, both back to 0 by 07:15:00/07:16:00.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and ready now; only ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 have a 07:02:17 start time (every other pod started 06:28:32–06:28:35 except flagd at 06:30:14), and every container reports restartCount 0 with ready true, with ad's and payment's container states empty lastState (no previous instance).

Deployments ad and payment currently report readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1 and metadata.generation 2, and Endpoints ad/payment resolve to the current pods 100.96.4.142 and 100.96.4.221 — so the Services do select these pods and the workloads are not degraded at read time.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo currently declares adFailure defaultVariant "on" ("Fail ad service") and paymentFailure defaultVariant "100%" ("Fail payment service charge requests n%"), while every other flag (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) is "off".

The ad and payment Deployment container specs contain no fault-injection, delay or error settings; their only feature-flag wiring is FLAGD_HOST=flagd and FLAGD_PORT=8013 (ad additionally OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp, payment OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT http://otel-collector:4317).

Most likely causal chain for the dominant error leg: the 07:02:17 rollout restart of Deployment ad removed its only pod; the replacement container, limited to cpu 50m, was throttled in 100% of CFS periods and needed 6m19s before it logged 'listening on 8080' (07:08:38 for a 07:02:19 container start), so frontend calls to Service ad:8080 hit the ClusterIP and were refused at TCP level, frontend returned HTTP 500 on GET / and /api/data, and the frontend error-span rate rose to 0.8667/s — which is what the RequestErrorRate warning reports. Alignment is exact: ad start of errors after the 07:02:20 kill, ad listening at 07:08:38, frontend error rate 0 from the 07:14:51 evaluation.

Second candidate with the same mechanism, smaller and earlier: the 07:02:17 restart of Deployment payment left its only pod unavailable until it served its first Charge at 07:03:57, and because payment is limited to cpu 20m (usage pinned at ~0.020 cores during startup, no log output before 07:03:57), checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls were refused and PlaceOrder plus frontend POST /api/checkout returned 500 until the checkout error series reached 0 by 07:10:00 — but the checkout error values collapse after 07:04, consistent with payment listening at 07:03:57.

Contributing configuration factor (not independently verified for the window): both pods have no readinessProbe and both Deployments run a single replica, so the container is counted ready as soon as it runs and the Service publishes an endpoint for a process that is not yet listening, and a rollout removes the only serving pod before its replacement can accept traffic. This would explain connection refused (backend reachable but no listener) rather than an empty-endpoint rejection.

Rejected as the cause of this burst: the flagd flags adFailure="on" and paymentFailure="100%". The failure path observed is a TCP-level connect refusal at the ad and payment Service ClusterIPs (grpc code 14 / dial tcp ... connection refused), which is not what an in-process feature-flag error injection produces, and the frontend error rate returned to 0 from the 07:14:51 evaluation while the ConfigMap still declares both faults when read at 07:20:32. It remains a separate anomaly worth confirming, and I could not verify what flagd was serving during the window.

Rejected: application crash, OOMKill or eviction of the ad or payment container. The old pods were deleted by their own ReplicaSets (SuccessfulDelete plus Deployment ScalingReplicaSet downscale) as part of a rollout, the new containers' lastState is empty with restartCount 0, and no OOMKilled or Evicted reason appears in the otel-demo events.

Rejected as the trigger: the tiny flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream error series on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation (0.0037 spans/s, present at 06:50–06:54 and again in separate minutes) is background noise; it is far below the frontend's failure volume, appears before the alerting deviation, and does not follow the frontend's error curve.

No node-level fault is indicated: the two restarted pods and most other otel-demo pods (accounting, currency, email, fraud-detection, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, otel-collector, postgresql, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) run on the same node i-0e9f8b08cc290a884, all are ready with restartCount 0 and none of them was recreated during the window; only the ad and payment pods carry the 07:02:17 start time and only their Deployments were rolled.

Give the ad container a realistic CPU budget (currently limits cpu 50m) or at minimum a startupProbe, so that a restart does not spend minutes throttled at 100% of CFS periods before it can bind port 8080; the same applies to payment (limits cpu 20m).

Add readinessProbes to ad and payment and run at least two replicas with a rolling-update strategy that keeps one ready pod (or use a surge/zero-unavailable pattern), so that a single-pod rollout cannot route traffic to a process that has not started listening.

Confirm who/what performed the 2026-11-17T07:02:17Z rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment, and confirm whether adFailure="on" and paymentFailure="100%" in flagd-config are intentional; both are outside what this Run can observe.

gaps: The alerting rule itself could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no data, so the exact expression, window and threshold behind 'RequestErrorRate' and the alert's 'current: 2.5777777777777775' value are unverified (the frontend error-span rates I measured at 07:03:51 were ~0.22 spans/s in total).

The exact first and last error seconds are not pinned: a 1-minute increase() query on the same frontend error span series returned zeros for 07:01:00–07:12:00, which contradicts the 5-minute rate series, so onset is bounded to the 06:58:51–07:03:51 evaluation window and the last error to 07:08:51–07:13:51.
Logs of the deleted ad pod ad-554b849958-mbnxm and payment pod payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb are unavailable ('previous instance not found'), so their shutdown behaviour cannot be inspected.
What triggered the 07:02:17Z rollout restart is not observable: the change_history integration is not integrated in this Run and no Kubernetes event names the actor.

flagd produced no readable log lines in 06:55–07:19:56 (all containers returned 0 lines), so I could not verify when flagd-config was last changed or which flag values flagd served during the window; Secrets are not readable.

kube_pod_status_ready queries returned no series for the ad and payment pods, so their readiness timeline during 07:02–07:10 is unknown; Endpoints and NetworkPolicy objects can only be read as current state (a NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned nothing, which is not evidence either way).
The kubectl rollout restart is documented only as a pod-template annotation; no owning change record ties it to a specific operator or pipeline.
next_steps: Ask the team/pipeline that owns otel-demo whether a deliberate restart of ad and payment ran at 2026-11-17T07:02:17Z, and why those two Deployments specifically.
Review the ad (cpu limit 50m) and payment (cpu limit 20m) resource settings and their missing readiness/startup probes with the platform owners; size CPU for JVM startup and add probes.

Verify the intended state of the flagd-config flags adFailure and paymentFailure with the demo owner, since both are declared as active faults even though they do not match this incident's failure path.
Add an alert/recording on kubectl rollout restarts of single-replica workloads so a restart that removes the only serving pod is visible before it becomes a request-error alert.
